gameplay.direct_outcome: Opened a direct My Aquarium screen. It showed an Aquarium/Nursery switch, level and coin counters, Tank health (hungry/algae/murk/waste), and Watch/Feed/Clean/Decorate/Shop modes. In Clean mode, the game instructed 'Drag across the glass to scrub with the Sponge'; two drag attempts showed a sponge/cursor effect but no attributable algae decrease. Murk measured 7% before clicking the clearly labeled Water change control. The game showed 'Fresh water is on its way!' and murk reached 0%; coin count stayed at 170 across that action. No Shop was opened and no currency was spent. Earlier balance change from 120 to 170 occurred over elapsed idle play and is not attributed to an input.

inputs_and_visible_responses.input: Opened Clean mode and selected the Sponge; dragged across the visible aquarium glass.
inputs_and_visible_responses.response: The sponge cursor/visual moved, but algae did not decrease in the immediate observed status; not counted as a cleaning success.

inputs_and_visible_responses.input: Clicked Water change (UI description: Clears murk) when murk was 7%.
inputs_and_visible_responses.response: A 'Fresh water is on its way!' toast appeared; the next state showed murk 0%. Coin count stayed 170.

gameplay.limits: Short management-game check; water-change response was verified, but the sponge action did not produce an isolated algae decrease. No Shop, purchase, full progression, or iframe was tested. AI attribution remains unverified under the explicit-AI gate.

ai_authorship_evidence.quote: One “GTA” prompt. 35 hours. Claude Opus 5.5 built a playable browser game with a living city and 28 story missions.

gameplay.load_observation: The creator page linked the playable benchmark build. Initial navigation was black for about 30 seconds before the neon sunset splash appeared; clicking it began shader compilation, then a 3D city spawn scene rendered.
gameplay.direct_outcome: In the 3D city scene, a one-second W input moved the avatar/camera forward toward the street. Pressing M opened the full Port Solana city map, showing named districts and a legend for police, shops, safehouses, races, roads, and turf; pressing M closed the map. The scene showed an avatar, pedestrians, traffic, storefronts, a minimap, an in-game clock, and $500 starting cash. A “CLICK TO PLAY” label remained visible while the movement and map controls responded; missions and vehicle entry were not tested.

inputs_and_visible_responses.visible_response: The avatar/camera advanced toward the street; the curb and nearby storefronts shifted in the view.

inputs_and_visible_responses.input: Pressed M.
inputs_and_visible_responses.visible_response: A full-screen Port Solana city map opened with districts, roads, destinations, and a legend.

inputs_and_visible_responses.input: Pressed M again.
inputs_and_visible_responses.visible_response: The map closed and the 3D city scene returned.

gameplay.limits: Short movement/map check only. The creator advertises 28 missions, but no mission, vehicle, combat, or full progression was tested.
